Downstream analysis for the networks created using FastSpar.

These scripts were written by Chen Xi Ye Xu as part of her Master´s Thesis 
for UAM - Master of Bioinformatics and Computational Biology. 

GEPHI INFO
After running this code we can use the results inside Gephi to visualize the network better!

In linux you download from Gephi (https://gephi.org/) the folder, unzip it, go to bin and then use ./gephi. If it doesn´t work, it is probably because you need to run chmod 777 gephi first. 

Gephi accepts .tsv files!

## 3) Loading FastSpar data.
```{r}
#Reading FastSpar correlation and p-value matrices.


##############################################################
#Function to clean taxonomy names with a hierarchical fallback.
##############################################################
clean_tax_name <- function(x) {
  #Split the full taxonomy string by semicolons.
  levels <- unlist(strsplit(x, ";\\s*"))

  #Names considered uninformative or unclassified.
  uninf_terms <- c("", "uncultured", "unclassified", "unknown",
                   "incertae_sedis", "ambiguous", "metagenome",
                   "_", "__", "___")

  #Walk backwards from genus to domain if the name is empty.
  chosen_name <- "Unclassified"

  for (lvl in rev(levels)) {
    #Remove rank prefixes like g__, f__, o__, etc.
    clean_val <- sub("^[a-zA-Z]+__?", "", lvl)
    clean_val <- trimws(clean_val)

    #Check if the level contains valid information.
    if (!(tolower(clean_val) %in% uninf_terms) && clean_val != "") {
      chosen_name <- clean_val
      break}}
  
  return(chosen_name)}


##############################################################
## Function to read and process FastSpar matrices.
##############################################################
load_fastspar <- function(CORR_FILE, PVAL_FILE) {

  #Reading correlation and p-value matrices.
  cor_mat <- as.matrix(read.table(CORR_FILE, header = TRUE, row.names = 1,
                                  sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE, comment.char = ""))

  p_mat <- as.matrix(read.table(PVAL_FILE, header = TRUE, row.names = 1,
                                sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE, comment.char = ""))


  #Validating that dimensions and names match perfectly.
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(cor_mat), rownames(p_mat)))
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(cor_mat), colnames(p_mat)))
  stopifnot(identical(rownames(cor_mat), colnames(cor_mat)))

  #Apply hierarchical cleaning to taxonomy names.
  cleaned_rownames <- sapply(rownames(cor_mat), clean_tax_name)

  #Ensure uniqueness across all row/column names.
  unique_rownames <- make.unique(cleaned_rownames, sep = "_")

  rownames(cor_mat) <- unique_rownames
  colnames(cor_mat) <- unique_rownames

  rownames(p_mat) <- unique_rownames
  colnames(p_mat) <- unique_rownames


  #Converting correlation and p-value matrices to long format edge lists.
  cor_df <- cor_mat %>%
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Taxon1") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-Taxon1, names_to = "Taxon2", values_to = "r")

  p_df <- p_mat %>%
    as.data.frame(check.names = FALSE) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Taxon1") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-Taxon1, names_to = "Taxon2", values_to = "p")


  #Joining correlation and p-values and applying significance 
  # and strength filters.
  r_cutoff <- 0.2
  p_cutoff <- 0.05

  edges_raw <- cor_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(p_df, by = c("Taxon1", "Taxon2")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Taxon1 < Taxon2,
      !is.na(r),
      !is.na(p),
      abs(r) >= r_cutoff,
      p <= p_cutoff
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(r > 0, "positive", "negative"))


  return(list(
    cor_mat = cor_mat,
    p_mat = p_mat,
    cor_df = cor_df,
    p_df = p_df,
    edges_raw = edges_raw
  ))}


##############################################################
## Process the three FastSpar analyses.
##############################################################

#WITHOUT sex separation.
ALL_RESULTS <- load_fastspar(ALL_CORR_FILE, ALL_PVAL_FILE)
ALL_COR_MAT <- ALL_RESULTS$cor_mat

cat("FINISHED 3) Loading FastSpar data.")
```

## 4) Filtering weaker connections.
```{r}
#Filtering parameters for a more focused, robust network.
r_cutoff <- 0.4

#Threshold must use adjusted p-value.
p_adj_cutoff <- 0.05

#Apply correction to p-values and filter significant correlations.
#   Benjamini-Hochberg = BH/fdr (more strict)
#   Holm = holm

filter_edges <- function(cor_df, p_df) {
  #Apply multiple-testing correction.
  p_df <- p_df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"))

  #Join correlations and adjusted p-values with stricter filters.
  edges_raw <- cor_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(p_df, by = c("Taxon1", "Taxon2")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Taxon1 < Taxon2,
      !is.na(r),
      !is.na(p_adj),
      abs(r) >= r_cutoff,
      p_adj <= p_adj_cutoff
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(sign = ifelse(r > 0, "positive", "negative"))

  return(list(
    p_df = p_df,
    edges_raw = edges_raw
  ))}


##############################################################
## Apply filtering to the three FastSpar analyses.
##############################################################

#WITHOUT sex separation.
ALL_FILTERED_RESULTS <- filter_edges(ALL_COR_DF, ALL_P_DF)
ALL_P_DF <- ALL_FILTERED_RESULTS$p_df
ALL_EDGES_RAW <- ALL_FILTERED_RESULTS$edges_raw


#FEMALE only.
FEMALE_FILTERED_RESULTS <- filter_edges(FEMALE_COR_DF, FEMALE_P_DF)
FEMALE_P_DF <- FEMALE_FILTERED_RESULTS$p_df
FEMALE_EDGES_RAW <- FEMALE_FILTERED_RESULTS$edges_raw


#MALE only.
MALE_FILTERED_RESULTS <- filter_edges(MALE_COR_DF, MALE_P_DF)
MALE_P_DF <- MALE_FILTERED_RESULTS$p_df
MALE_EDGES_RAW <- MALE_FILTERED_RESULTS$edges_raw


cat("FINISHED 4) Filtering weaker connections.")
```


## 5) General statistical assessment of the networks.
```{r}
##############################################################
## Function to analyse the results from filtering.
##############################################################
diagnose_network <- function(cor_df, p_df, analysis_name) {

  results <- cor_df %>%
    dplyr::left_join(p_df, by = c("Taxon1", "Taxon2")) %>%
    dplyr::filter(Taxon1 < Taxon2, !is.na(r), !is.na(p_adj))

  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("ANALYSIS:", analysis_name, "\n")
  cat("========================================\n")

  cat("Total unique taxon pairs:", nrow(results), "\n")

  if (nrow(results) == 0) {
    cat("No valid taxon pairs available for assessment.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))}

  cat("Pairs with |r| >=", r_cutoff, ":",
      sum(abs(results$r) >= r_cutoff), "\n")

  cat("Pairs with adjusted p <=", p_adj_cutoff, ":",
      sum(results$p_adj <= p_adj_cutoff), "\n")

  cat("Pairs passing both thresholds:",
      sum(abs(results$r) >= r_cutoff &
          results$p_adj <= p_adj_cutoff), "\n")

  cat("Pairs with raw p <= 0.05:",
      sum(results$p <= 0.05), "\n")

  cat("Maximum absolute correlation:",
      max(abs(results$r), na.rm = TRUE), "\n")

  cat("Minimum adjusted p-value:",
      min(results$p_adj, na.rm = TRUE), "\n")}


##############################################################
## Assess the three FastSpar analyses.
##############################################################

#WITHOUT sex separation.
diagnose_network(ALL_COR_DF, ALL_P_DF, "ALL")

#FEMALE only.
diagnose_network(FEMALE_COR_DF, FEMALE_P_DF, "FEMALE")

#MALE only.
diagnose_network(MALE_COR_DF, MALE_P_DF, "MALE")


cat("FINISHED 5) General statistical assessment of the networks.\n")
```














## 6) Creating node and edge tables for Gephi export and network construction.
```{r}
##############################################################
## Function to format edge tables.
##############################################################
make_edges <- function(edges_raw) {

  edges_all <- data.frame(
    Source = edges_raw$Taxon1,
    Target = edges_raw$Taxon2,
    Type = rep("Undirected", nrow(edges_raw)),
    Weight = round(abs(edges_raw$r), 6),
    r = round(edges_raw$r, 6),
    p = signif(edges_raw$p, 6),
    p_adj = signif(edges_raw$p_adj, 6),
    sign = edges_raw$sign,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  #Splitting into positive and negative edge subsets.
  edges_pos <- dplyr::filter(edges_all, sign == "positive")
  edges_neg <- dplyr::filter(edges_all, sign == "negative")

  return(list(
    edges_all = edges_all,
    edges_pos = edges_pos,
    edges_neg = edges_neg
  ))}


##############################################################
## Function to calculate node degrees and strengths dynamically.
##############################################################
make_nodes <- function(edges_df) {

  if (nrow(edges_df) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      Id = character(),
      Label = character(),
      Degree = integer(),
      Strength = numeric(),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))}

  nds <- unique(c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target))
  deg <- table(c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target))
  str <- tapply(rep(edges_df$Weight, 2),
                c(edges_df$Source, edges_df$Target), sum)

  out <- data.frame(
    Id = nds,
    Label = nds,
    Degree = as.integer(deg[nds]),
    Strength = round(as.numeric(str[nds]), 6),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  out$Degree[is.na(out$Degree)] <- 0L
  out$Strength[is.na(out$Strength)] <- 0

  return(out)}


##############################################################
## Generate edge and node tables for each analysis.
##############################################################

#WITHOUT sex separation.
ALL_EDGES <- make_edges(ALL_EDGES_RAW)

ALL_EDGES_ALL <- ALL_EDGES$edges_all
ALL_EDGES_POS <- ALL_EDGES$edges_pos
ALL_EDGES_NEG <- ALL_EDGES$edges_neg

ALL_NODES_ALL <- make_nodes(ALL_EDGES_ALL)
ALL_NODES_POS <- make_nodes(ALL_EDGES_POS)
ALL_NODES_NEG <- make_nodes(ALL_EDGES_NEG)


#FEMALE only.
FEMALE_EDGES <- make_edges(FEMALE_EDGES_RAW)

FEMALE_EDGES_ALL <- FEMALE_EDGES$edges_all
FEMALE_EDGES_POS <- FEMALE_EDGES$edges_pos
FEMALE_EDGES_NEG <- FEMALE_EDGES$edges_neg

FEMALE_NODES_ALL <- make_nodes(FEMALE_EDGES_ALL)
FEMALE_NODES_POS <- make_nodes(FEMALE_EDGES_POS)
FEMALE_NODES_NEG <- make_nodes(FEMALE_EDGES_NEG)


#MALE only.
MALE_EDGES <- make_edges(MALE_EDGES_RAW)

MALE_EDGES_ALL <- MALE_EDGES$edges_all
MALE_EDGES_POS <- MALE_EDGES$edges_pos
MALE_EDGES_NEG <- MALE_EDGES$edges_neg

MALE_NODES_ALL <- make_nodes(MALE_EDGES_ALL)
MALE_NODES_POS <- make_nodes(MALE_EDGES_POS)
MALE_NODES_NEG <- make_nodes(MALE_EDGES_NEG)


##############################################################
## Summary of generated node and edge tables.
##############################################################
message("WITHOUT separation - Total edges: ", nrow(ALL_EDGES_ALL),
        " | Positive: ", nrow(ALL_EDGES_POS),
        " | Negative: ", nrow(ALL_EDGES_NEG))

message("FEMALE only - Total edges: ", nrow(FEMALE_EDGES_ALL),
        " | Positive: ", nrow(FEMALE_EDGES_POS),
        " | Negative: ", nrow(FEMALE_EDGES_NEG))

message("MALE only - Total edges: ", nrow(MALE_EDGES_ALL),
        " | Positive: ", nrow(MALE_EDGES_POS),
        " | Negative: ", nrow(MALE_EDGES_NEG))


cat("FINISHED 6) Creating node and edge tables for Gephi export and network construction.\n")
```


## 7) Exporting edge and node tables for all, positive and negative networks.
```{r}
##############################################################
## Function to export edge and node tables.
##############################################################
export_gephi <- function(EDGES_ALL, EDGES_POS, EDGES_NEG,
                         NODES_ALL, NODES_POS, NODES_NEG, GEPHI_DIR) {

  #Creating subdirectories inside the Gephi folder.
  dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Positive"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  #Writing edge tables to Gephi folder.
  write.table(EDGES_ALL, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All", "fastspar_genus_edges_all.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  write.table(EDGES_POS, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Positive", "fastspar_genus_edges_positive.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  write.table(EDGES_NEG, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative", "fastspar_genus_edges_negative.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  #Writing node tables to Gephi folder.
  write.table(NODES_ALL, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "All", "fastspar_genus_nodes_all.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  write.table(NODES_POS, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Positive", "fastspar_genus_nodes_positive.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  write.table(NODES_NEG, file.path(GEPHI_DIR, "Negative", "fastspar_genus_nodes_negative.tsv"),
              sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

  message("Gephi tables successfully exported to: ", GEPHI_DIR)}


##############################################################
## Export WITHOUT sex separation.
##############################################################
export_gephi(
  ALL_EDGES_ALL, ALL_EDGES_POS, ALL_EDGES_NEG,
  ALL_NODES_ALL, ALL_NODES_POS, ALL_NODES_NEG,
  file.path(WITHOUT_DIR, "Gephi"))


##############################################################
## Export FEMALE only.
##############################################################
export_gephi(
  FEMALE_EDGES_ALL, FEMALE_EDGES_POS, FEMALE_EDGES_NEG,
  FEMALE_NODES_ALL, FEMALE_NODES_POS, FEMALE_NODES_NEG,
  file.path(FEMALE_DIR, "Gephi"))


##############################################################
## Export MALE only.
##############################################################
export_gephi(
  MALE_EDGES_ALL, MALE_EDGES_POS, MALE_EDGES_NEG,
  MALE_NODES_ALL, MALE_NODES_POS, MALE_NODES_NEG,
  file.path(MALE_DIR, "Gephi"))


cat("FINISHED 7) Exporting edge and node tables for all, positive and negative networks.\n")
```


## 8) Plotting correlation networks.
```{r}
##############################################################
## Function to plot correlation networks using ggraph.
##############################################################
plot_correlation_network <- function(edges_out, title, outfile_prefix) {
  for (sign_label in c("positive", "negative")) {
    edges_sub <- subset(edges_out, sign == sign_label)

    if (nrow(edges_sub) == 0) {
      message("No ", sign_label, " edges to plot: ", outfile_prefix)
      next}

    nodes_sub <- tibble::tibble(
      name = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)),
      label = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)))

    g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
      d = edges_sub[, c("Source", "Target", "r", "Weight")],
      vertices = nodes_sub,
      directed = FALSE)

    V(g)$degree <- igraph::degree(g)
    g_tbl <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(g)

    edge_color <- if (sign_label == "positive") "firebrick3" else "steelblue3"

    p <- ggraph::ggraph(g_tbl, layout = "fr") +
      ggraph::geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), color = edge_color, alpha = 0.4) +
      ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
      ggraph::geom_node_point(aes(size = degree), color = "grey20", alpha = 0.9) +
      ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), guide = "none") +
      ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf) +
      ggraph::theme_graph() +
      ggplot2::labs(title = title, subtitle = paste(sign_label, "correlations"))

    outfile <- paste0(outfile_prefix, "_", sign_label, ".png")

    ggplot2::ggsave(outfile, plot = p, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300)

    message("Figure saved: ", outfile)
  }}


##############################################################
## Plot WITHOUT sex separation.
##############################################################
plot_correlation_network(
  edges_out = ALL_EDGES_ALL,
  title = "FastSpar Genus Correlation Network - All Samples",
  outfile_prefix = file.path(WITHOUT_DIR, "Figures", "fastspar_genus"))


##############################################################
## Plot FEMALE only.
##############################################################
plot_correlation_network(
  edges_out = FEMALE_EDGES_ALL,
  title = "FastSpar Genus Correlation Network - Female",
  outfile_prefix = file.path(FEMALE_DIR, "Figures", "fastspar_genus"))


##############################################################
## Plot MALE only.
##############################################################
plot_correlation_network(
  edges_out = MALE_EDGES_ALL,
  title = "FastSpar Genus Correlation Network - Male",
  outfile_prefix = file.path(MALE_DIR, "Figures", "fastspar_genus"))


cat("FINISHED 8) Plotting correlation networks.\n")
```

## 9) Plot the network interactively in R!
```{r}
#Select the analysis here: "ALL", "FEMALE" or "MALE".
analysis_type <- "MALE"

#Select the correlation sign here: "positive" or "negative".
sign_type <- "negative"


##############################################################
## Select the corresponding edge table.
##############################################################
edges_selected <- switch(
  analysis_type,
  "ALL" = ALL_EDGES_ALL,
  "FEMALE" = FEMALE_EDGES_ALL,
  "MALE" = MALE_EDGES_ALL,
  stop("Invalid analysis_type. Choose ALL, FEMALE or MALE!!"))

edges_sub <- subset(edges_selected, sign == sign_type)


##############################################################
## Prepare network data.
##############################################################
if (nrow(edges_sub) == 0) {
  stop("No ", sign_type, " edges available for ", analysis_type, " analysis.")}

#Function to strip all higher taxonomy levels and prefixes (e.g., g__).
clean_tax_name <- function(x) {
  x <- sub(".*;\\s*", "", x)
  x <- sub("^[a-zA-Z]+__?", "", x)
  return(x)}

#Clean Source and Target columns.
edges_sub$Source <- clean_tax_name(edges_sub$Source)
edges_sub$Target <- clean_tax_name(edges_sub$Target)

nodes_sub <- tibble::tibble(
  name = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)),
  label = unique(c(edges_sub$Source, edges_sub$Target)))

g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(
  d = edges_sub[, c("Source", "Target", "r", "Weight")],
  vertices = nodes_sub,
  directed = FALSE)

V(g)$degree <- igraph::degree(g)
g_tbl <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(g)


##############################################################
## Plot network interactively in RStudio.
##############################################################

#Dynamic styling and labels based on selected analysis and sign.
edge_color <- if (sign_type == "positive") "firebrick3" else "steelblue3"

net_title <- paste0(
  "FastSpar ",
  tools::toTitleCase(analysis_type),
  " ",
  tools::toTitleCase(sign_type),
  " Correlation Network")

net_sub <- paste(analysis_type, sign_type, "correlations at genus level")

#Render the plot directly in the RStudio plot window.
ggraph::ggraph(g_tbl, layout = "fr") +
  ggraph::geom_edge_link(aes(width = Weight), color = edge_color, alpha = 0.4) +
  ggraph::scale_edge_width(range = c(0.2, 2), guide = "none") +
  ggraph::geom_node_point(aes(size = degree), color = "grey20", alpha = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 8), guide = "none") +
  ggraph::geom_node_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  ggraph::theme_graph() +
  ggplot2::labs(title = net_title, subtitle = net_sub)


cat("FINISHED 9) Plotting the network interactively in RStudio!\n")
```
